documentation.content:
The nightly fitPatternsV2 run has not reported a completed scan.

WHY THIS POLICY EXISTS. It is the third instance of the shape scheduledDuelReveals-silent.json exists for, and it was missing until an audit counted the schedules against the policies: five policies, and neither of the two nightly jobs among them. A scheduled function that stops running reports NOTHING — no error, no page, no failed request — because the failure is an absence. Everything downstream keeps serving whatever it last published, so the console stays green and the app looks healthy while the number on screen ages.

WHAT IT WATCHES. The log-based metric `patterns_fit`, which functions/src/patterns.ts already emitted before this policy existed — the emit side was never the gap. A THRESHOLD over a trailing 24 hours rather than an absence — see below; the cron is 02:37 UTC daily.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE. the Patterns tab has no other source: v2_patterns/loadings is what the Map places questions by and what the Oracle estimates from, and a fit that stops running leaves the tab drawing a model that quietly ages.

FIRST RESPONSE. Check Cloud Scheduler for the job's last execution and its status, then the function's own logs for the run that should have happened. A run that STARTED and threw shows up in the errors, not here; this policy is specifically for the run that never began — a paused scheduler job, a failed deploy that dropped the trigger, or a quota block. check:deploy-targets and check:fn-runtime cover the deploy-side causes at commit time, so a fire here after a green deploy points at the scheduler or the project, not the code.

WHY THIS IS A THRESHOLD AND NOT AN ABSENCE, which is the arithmetic that
decides it. Cloud Monitoring refuses any `conditionAbsent.duration` over
**23h30m (84600s)** — a server-side ceiling that appears in neither the v3
discovery document nor alert.proto, both of which state only a 120s
minimum. It is real: the first `--apply` run met it after the
`resource.type` fix, and six independent public repositories record it,
several as live-verified.

That ceiling makes an absence condition **unable to express this policy at
all**. The cron is 02:37 UTC daily, so the healthy gap between two runs is
86400s — LONGER than the longest window the API will accept. Any absence
policy here goes true for the ~30 minutes between the 84600s mark and the
next run, every single morning. An alert that pages daily is one the
operator learns to delete, which is the failure `DEPLOYMENT.md § Alerting`
opens by refusing.

So the shape changed instead of the number: count the runs in a trailing
24 hours and fire when there are none. `ALIGN_SUM` over an 86400s
alignment period (the alerting maximum is 90000s), `COMPARISON_LT 1`, held
for an hour. On a healthy day that sum is 1 and the condition never goes
true; on a missed run it is 0.

`evaluationMissingData: EVALUATION_MISSING_DATA_ACTIVE` is what keeps the
absence half. A threshold over a series that has stopped emitting entirely
— the function deleted, the trigger dropped — would otherwise evaluate
nothing and stay green forever, which is the exact hole the absence
condition existed to close. ACTIVE treats missing data as the condition
being met. It requires a `duration` of at least 60s, which is why the hour
is not zero.

SINCE D387 THE FIT RUNS INSIDE `digestEngagementV2` (functions/src/nightly.ts), the one nightly pass that reads yesterday's ledger once for the engagement digest, this fit and the taste fold. The scheduled function `fitPatternsV2` is retired from the source; this policy keeps its name because the display name is what the armed policy is keyed on, and it keeps working because the pass emits `patterns_fit` only when the fit itself completed — a fit that threw leaves the other folds running and this metric silent, which is exactly the condition to page on. So a fire here after D387 means the fit failed or the whole pass never ran: check `digestEngagementV2`'s scheduler job and its logs, where a failed fold is an ERROR line carrying `metric: nightly_fold_failed` and `fold: patterns`.
